_doc: Allowlist for yarn audit high/critical advisories that cannot be fixed in the current branch. Every entry needs a reason and a review date. See SUPPLY-CHAIN-SECURITY.md §6.

_fields.id: npm advisory numeric ID (from `yarn audit --json` advisory.id)
_fields.ghsa: GitHub Security Advisory ID, for humans — not used for matching
_fields.reason: why the advisory is allowlisted — upstream has no fix, major version bump deferred, not on a reachable code path, etc.
_fields.added: YYYY-MM-DD when the entry was added
_fields.review: YYYY-MM-DD by which the entry must be re-evaluated. An expired entry prints a CI warning but does not fail the job.

entries.reason: DoS (quadratic CPU on crafted YAML merge-key chains) reachable only via nx build-time tooling (@nx/next > nx > js-yaml 4.x), which parses our own trusted config files and is not shipped in the Next.js runtime bundle. No untrusted-input path. A blanket js-yaml resolution to >=4.3.0 is unsafe because the 3.x line under @yarnpkg/parsers uses the safeLoad API removed in 4.x.

Same GHSA on the js-yaml 3.x line, reached via nx build-time tooling (@nx/next > nx > @yarnpkg/parsers > js-yaml 3.x). Build-time only, trusted input, not in the shipped runtime. Cannot be co-resolved with the 4.x consumer via a single Yarn resolution without breaking API compatibility.

CVE-2026-59870 (quadratic CPU in !!omap resolution) on the js-yaml 3.x line, reached only via nx build-time tooling (@nx/next > nx > @yarnpkg/parsers > js-yaml 3.x). Build-time only, parses our own trusted config, not in the shipped runtime. Same co-resolution constraint as 1123912: the 3.x consumer uses the safeLoad API removed in 4.x, so a single Yarn resolution cannot fix both lines.

Same CVE-2026-59870 on the js-yaml 4.x line, reached only via nx build-time tooling (@nx/next > nx > js-yaml 4.x). Build-time only, trusted input, not in the shipped runtime. See 1123911 for why a blanket js-yaml resolution is unsafe.

maxTotalMergeKeys does not limit CPU use for empty merge sources, on the js-yaml 3.x line reached only via nx build-time tooling (@nx/next > @nx/workspace > nx > @yarnpkg/parsers > js-yaml 3.x). Build-time only, parses our own trusted config, not in the shipped runtime. Same co-resolution constraint as 1123912 and 1138114: the 3.x consumer uses the safeLoad API removed in 4.x, so a single Yarn resolution cannot fix both lines.

Same advisory on the js-yaml 4.x line, reached only via nx build-time tooling (@nx/next > @nx/workspace > nx > js-yaml 4.x). Build-time only, trusted input, not in the shipped runtime. See 1123911 for why a blanket js-yaml resolution is unsafe. Review together with the other js-yaml entries by 2026-10-23.
